title: Git's secret diary
concept: git reflog brings back a lost commit

story.speaker: Sam
story.text: I think I deleted a whole afternoon of work. The sponsors page is gone.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Probably not gone. Git keeps a private diary of everywhere HEAD has been.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: It is called the **reflog**. Run `git reflog` and read it.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Every line has a short code like `abc1234`. That is a commit you can go back to.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Find the commit that added the sponsors page, then bring the branch back to it.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `git reset --hard <code>` is the normal rescue here. It is safe because we are moving *forward* to work we lost.

hints: The commit still exists, it just has no branch pointing at it. Find it in the reflog.
`git reflog` lists where HEAD has been, newest first. Find the line mentioning the sponsors page and copy its code.
Run `git reflog`, find the line for "Add sponsors page", then run `git reset --hard HEAD@{1}`.
recap: `git reflog` lists everywhere HEAD has been, so a commit with no branch on it can still be found and recovered.

cheatSheet.summary: Move the branch back to that commit

predict.question: The commit has no branch pointing at it. Is it really gone?

choices.text: Yes, with no branch it is deleted immediately
No, it is still stored and the reflog remembers it

predict.explanation: Git keeps commits for weeks even with no branch on them. The reflog is how you find them again.
